notes: Windows event detection rules. Each rule is evaluated against parsed EVTX records. Conditions use field names from <EventData>/<UserData>. 'prerequisites' documents the audit policy a rule depends on: absence of matching events does not prove absence of activity.

rules.title: Repeated failed logons for the same account
rules.description: Three or more failed logons (4625) for the same account from the same source within five minutes.
rules.rationale: Consistent with password guessing. Also produced by users mistyping passwords, stale saved credentials or misconfigured services.

rules.title: Successful logon recorded
rules.description: An account logged on (4624). Logon type and source are recorded for timeline context.
rules.rationale: Routine activity; establishes who was using the host and when.

rules.title: Process executed from a user-writable location
rules.description: A process image was launched from Downloads, AppData, Desktop, ProgramData or a Temp directory.
rules.rationale: Malware is frequently staged in user-writable directories. Portable apps, installers and updaters also run from these paths.

rules.title: Executable with a document-style double extension was run
rules.description: The executed image name ends in a document extension followed by an executable extension.
rules.rationale: Double extensions disguise executables as documents when Windows hides known extensions; rare in legitimate software.

rules.title: PowerShell launched with encoded command or hidden window
rules.description: powershell.exe/pwsh.exe started with -EncodedCommand (or abbreviation) and/or a hidden window.
rules.rationale: Encoding hides the script from command-line inspection. Some management agents use the same flags; decode and review the command.
rules.prerequisites: Audit Process Creation enabled AND 'Include command line in process creation events' policy enabled; otherwise CommandLine is empty and this rule cannot fire.

rules.title: Process spawned by a binary in a user-writable location
rules.description: The parent process image lives in a user-writable directory.
rules.rationale: Child processes of recently downloaded binaries show what the binary did on the host.
rules.prerequisites: Audit Process Creation enabled (ParentProcessName is present on Windows 10 / Server 2016 and later).

rules.title: PowerShell script block with collection, staging or transfer keywords
rules.description: A logged PowerShell script block contains keywords associated with archiving, uploading, log clearing or dynamic code execution.
rules.rationale: Keyword matches show capability, not intent; review the full script block. Administrators use the same cmdlets.
rules.prerequisites: PowerShell Script Block Logging enabled, or the block was automatically logged as suspicious (Level 3/Warning).

rules.title: PowerShell script block recorded
rules.description: A PowerShell script block was logged.
rules.rationale: Provides visibility into executed PowerShell for timeline context.

rules.title: Scheduled task created
rules.rationale: Scheduled tasks are a common persistence mechanism; software installers also create them. Review the task action.
rules.prerequisites: Audit Other Object Access Events enabled.

rules.title: Service installed
rules.rationale: Services provide SYSTEM-level persistence. Legitimate software installs services too; review the image path.
rules.prerequisites: Logged by the Service Control Manager by default.

rules.title: Service installed with binary in a user-writable or ProgramData path
rules.description: The installed service's binary resides outside Program Files / System32.
rules.rationale: Legitimate services are usually installed under Program Files or System32.
rules.prerequisites: Logged by the Service Control Manager by default.

rules.title: Local user account created
rules.rationale: Attackers create accounts for persistence; verify against change-management records.

rules.title: Member added to the local Administrators group
rules.description: A security principal was added to BUILTIN\Administrators (4732, target SID S-1-5-32-544).
rules.rationale: Grants full control of the host. Verify against change-management records.

rules.title: Security audit log cleared
rules.rationale: Clearing the Security log destroys evidence; rarely part of routine operations.
rules.prerequisites: Always logged when the Security log is cleared.

rules.title: Event log cleared
rules.description: A non-Security event log was cleared (System 104). The cleared channel is recorded in UserData.
rules.rationale: Log clearing removes evidence of activity. Administrators occasionally clear logs during troubleshooting.
rules.prerequisites: Logged by the Event Log service by default.

rules.title: Access to a file in a sensitive location
rules.description: An object-access audit event records access to a file under a folder configured as sensitive.
rules.rationale: Access alone is not misuse; the accessing process and timing determine relevance.
rules.prerequisites: Audit File System enabled AND a SACL configured on the folder; without both, file reads are not logged.

rules.title: Outbound connection to an external address permitted
rules.description: Windows Filtering Platform permitted an outbound connection to an address outside internal ranges (5156). Documentation ranges (RFC 5737) used in simulated data count as external.
rules.rationale: Records which process opened which outbound connection; relevance depends on the destination and process.
rules.prerequisites: Audit Filtering Platform Connection enabled (high volume; often disabled).

rules.title: Outbound connection by PowerShell or a binary in a user-writable path
rules.description: PowerShell or a binary located in a user-writable directory connected to an external address.
rules.rationale: Script hosts and freshly downloaded binaries making external connections warrant review.
